metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward by 1–3% for days 1–5.
- After a price spike (e.g., >45), model tends to overshoot and then undercorrect; apply a “cool-down” bias: reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — overcorrects toward prior mean; add a “sentiment-adjusted drift” term: if sentiment = 0, forecast = prior 7-day average + 0.5×(true - prior avg) for next 3 days.
- Model underestimates late-period (days 20–30) prices when true outcomes show sustained upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for days 20–25 if prior 5-day avg > 45.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2 consecutive days, model is likely underestimating supply/demand shock — increase next forecast by 2–4% and apply a “lagged correction” rule: if true > forecast, next forecast = true + 0.3×(true - forecast) for 3 days.
- Sentiment history is always 0.00 — no emotional signal — so no sentiment-based adjustment is triggered; model must rely on pure technical/price momentum rules.
